Volume
vol'yum
n. (a roll or scroll of writing; in Psalm 40 and Hebrews 10, the book in which the Son's obedience was written before He came)
Latin volumen, a roll, from volvere, to roll — a book was a scroll before it was a codex. The Hebrew in Psalm 40:7 is megillah, a roll; the Greek in Hebrews 10:7 is kephalis, properly the knob or head of the roller round which the scroll was wound.

Biblical Definition

“Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me” (Psalm 40:7). The Psalm is David's, and Hebrews takes it as Christ's own words spoken on entering the world: “Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God” (Hebrews 10:7). The setting matters. The writer has just quoted the line that God did not desire sacrifice and offering but prepared a body (Hebrews 10:5), and he draws the conclusion in the next verse: “He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second” (Hebrews 10:9). The whole apparatus of bulls and goats is removed to make room for an obedience. What the volume contained was not merely predictions to be checked off but a will to be done — and the Son came saying that the roll was written about Him and that He had come to perform it. David's own line completes the sense: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart” (Psalm 40:8). Here is the active obedience of Christ in a single figure. The book was written before He came; He came to do what was written; and by that will believers are sanctified.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines volume as a roll, as the ancients wrote on strips rolled on a stick, hence a book of a certain size.

expand to see more

VOLUME, n. A roll; a book; primarily, a roll or turn, as the ancients wrote on long strips of bark or parchment, which they rolled on a stick.

2. A book, or a collection of sheets of paper bound together.

3. Dimensions; compass; space occupied, as of a body.

SCROLL, n. A roll of paper or parchment; or a writing formed into a roll.

MEGILLAH, Heb. a roll or volume.

Key Scripture

Hebrews 10:7 — "Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God."

Psalm 40:7 — "Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me,"

Psalm 40:8 — "I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart."

Hebrews 10:9 — "Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second."

Modern Corruption

The volume is treated as a book of predictions to be verified, when Hebrews reads it as a will to be performed by the Son.

expand to see more

Prophecy is often handled as though its whole function were evidential — a list of forecasts whose fulfilment proves the case. Hebrews 10 does something else with the volume. What is written in the roll is the Father's will, and the Son's answer is not this predicts me but I come to do it. Reduce Scripture to a prediction-checklist and the doctrine that this passage exists to teach — that Christ's obedience, not merely His death, is the substance of our acceptance — drops out entirely. The volume is about a will performed, and the performing is the gospel.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the active obedience of Christ. It has been quietly surrendered wherever the atonement is preached as though only the last six hours mattered, and it was denied outright by those in the seventeenth century who allowed Christ's suffering to be imputed but not His law-keeping. The Reformed confessions hold the whole: the righteousness imputed to the believer is the righteousness of a life lived under the law as well as a death died under its curse. Lo, I come to do thy will — and He did the whole of it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew megillah, a roll — Psalm 40:7, Jeremiah 36; Greek kephalis (G2777), the head of a scroll-roller — Hebrews 10:7, its only occurrence.

expand to see more

Hebrew megillah — a roll or volume; Psalm 40:7, and the roll Jehoiakim cut with a penknife in Jeremiah 36.

Greek kephalis (G2777) — the knob at the head of a scroll-roller, hence the roll itself; Hebrews 10:7, its only occurrence.

Greek biblion (G975) — book, scroll; joined to kephalis in Hebrews 10:7 as the volume of the book.

Greek thelema (G2307) — will; Hebrews 10:7, 9, 10 — the will written, the will done, and the will by which we are sanctified.

Hebrews 10:10 draws the conclusion: by the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

Usage

"“In the volume of the book it is written of me” — the Son on entering the world."

"“Lo, I come to do thy will, O God” — prophecy as commission, not merely forecast."

"The roll was written first; the obedience answered it."
